first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent this because she has her eye on my veil. The intro promises 'whether to wear a family veil, and how a veil behaves on a windy clifftop', which is exactly our conversation, so I kept going. Calm, grown-up tone, short paragraphs, easy on the iPad.

journey.quote: A veil borrowed from a happily married bride has long been counted lucky, which makes a family veil both something borrowed and an heirloom.
journey.reaction: Well, that's lovely. Thirty-four years married, so I think mine qualifies.

journey.section: 2. History of the wedding veil in ancient Rome
journey.quote: Her hair was arranged in six locks with woollen fillets, she wore a straight white woven tunic fastened at the waist with a "knot of Hercules", and over it all a great flame-coloured veil.
journey.reaction: Interesting, but the Romans and the medieval wimple take a while before we get to anything I can act on. I'd skim this part on a second read.

journey.section: 4. Queen Victoria and the white lace veil
journey.quote: On her head she wore a wreath of the same blossoms, over which, but not so as to conceal her face, a beautiful veil of Honiton lace was thrown.
journey.reaction: I enjoyed that. Nice to read something that quotes The Times rather than an influencer.

journey.section: 6. Who lifts the veil, and when
journey.quote: A mother or father lifts it as they hand over, so the bride stands at the altar with her face clear.
journey.reaction: I hadn't thought the mother could do it. I'll be raising that with my daughter.

journey.quote: Agree with the owner how the veil will be worn, who carries it there, and when it goes home.
journey.reaction: Thank you. That's me, the owner, and it treats my questions as sensible rather than fussy.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, standard travel insurance policies typically don't cover items stolen from checked baggage on an airline, train or bus, or items left unattended.
journey.reaction: Didn't know that. This is the bit I'll forward to my husband.

journey.quote: If the veil belongs to someone else, ask whether their own insurance covers it overseas before it leaves home.
journey.reaction: Fair point. I'll ring our insurer this week.

journey.quote: One person plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments, as your single point of contact.
journey.reaction: Payments caught my eye. But it doesn't say whether deposits to overseas suppliers are protected, or whether quotes are in Australian dollars.

journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and your advisor confirms the inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: In writing, before anything starts. Good. I'd still want a phone call before we pay a cent.

unanswered_questions: Are quotes in Australian dollars, and are deposits paid to overseas venues and suppliers protected?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong on the day overseas, at 2am their time?
Is the first step a phone conversation with the Wedded Advisor before anything is booked?
On the wedding morning, who looks after the family veil while my daughter is dressing, and is there somewhere safe at the venue to keep it?
would_share_with: My husband, with the 'Travelling with your veil' section marked, especially the checked baggage and insurance lines
My daughter, to agree whether my veil goes, who carries it and who lifts it

cta_reaction.quote: You will work with one Wedded Advisor, your single point of contact from the first conversation to the wedding day.
cta_reaction.why: One named contact and the fee in writing reassure me. This is really an article about veils, though, so I'd click if my daughter asked, and only if I knew a real person would ring before anything is paid.

top_3_changes: In the closing section, say plainly that the first step is a phone conversation with the advisor, before anything is booked.
In 'Wearing a family veil' or the destination section, add one line on who holds the heirloom veil on the wedding morning, framed as a question to ask the venue or planner.
Tighten sections 2 and 3 (Rome, late antiquity, the wimple) slightly so practical readers reach the family veil and travel advice sooner.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent, practical, reads top to bottom)
No invented brand facts; missing business details listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments, image slots and VERIFY markers treated as invisible
Title and deferred business details not raised as must-fix, per orchestrator

open_questions.question: AUD quotes, deposit protection and on-the-day contact remain this persona's trust gaps, but business details are deferred. Treat as nice-to-have?

assumptions: Margaret reads the whole article on an iPad because her daughter sent it, and she owns the family veil in question.
Per orchestrator, brand voice does not discuss sourcing; the history comment is about reading length, not sourcing.
